security_audit.summary: All 26 static findings are false positives. They result from Markdown inline code and documentation paths, not Ruby, shell, or reconnaissance behavior. The skill does document a security-sensitive trusted-rendering opt-out that can reduce protections when its trust boundary is misapplied.

remediation.issue: Trusted rendering guidance permits disabling HTML and Mermaid protections.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit trust-boundary review, keep the opt-out limited to known static content, and warn against using it with user-controlled or streamed input.

content.value_statement: Angular teams need a clear path for adding Markdown rendering without unsafe defaults or unnecessary dependencies. This skill guides standalone setup, streaming behavior, CSS imports, and explicit trusted-content boundaries.
actual_capabilities: Checks that the host repository uses Angular before integration.
Guides standalone component imports for MarkstreamAngularComponent.
Explains required Markstream and optional KaTeX stylesheet imports.
Configures content bindings, streaming states, and final-state behavior.
Explains smooth streaming, fade, and typewriter presentation options.
Documents safe HTML, strict Mermaid, and trusted custom-tag boundaries.
limitations: It does not install packages or run build commands without tool approval.
It does not provide a complete application architecture or backend streaming service.
Trusted HTML and non-strict Mermaid settings require a separate security review.
It relies on the installed markstream-angular version and repository configuration.

use_cases.title: Add Markdown to a standalone app
use_cases.description: Set up a standalone Angular component with Markstream imports, content binding, and required styles.

use_cases.title: Build a streaming chat view
use_cases.description: Configure smooth streaming, cursor behavior, fade settings, and the final state for an AI chat interface.

use_cases.title: Migrate a trusted legacy renderer
use_cases.description: Preserve a documented trusted rendering workflow while keeping safe defaults for all other content.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Add markstream-angular to this Angular app. Use a standalone component, bind a Markdown string to content, and list the required stylesheet imports.

prompt_templates.title: Add math support
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate markstream-angular with optional KaTeX support. Keep dependencies minimal and show where each stylesheet belongs.

prompt_templates.title: Configure streaming chat
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Angular chat message component using markstream-angular. Configure streaming, fade, typewriter, and final-state behavior for live and recovered messages.

prompt_templates.title: Review a trusted renderer
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Angular markstream integration. Keep safe HTML and strict Mermaid defaults, then identify any narrowly justified trusted-content exceptions and document their boundaries.

output_examples.input: Add a basic Markdown message component to my Angular application.
output: The component import and content binding to use.

output_examples.input: My chat shows live tokens and later reloads complete history.
output: Streaming uses smooth pacing with the cursor enabled.
Recovered history disables pacing and uses fade animation.
The final flag marks completion after visible content catches up.

output_examples.input: Can I allow custom HTML tags in Markdown?
output: Use custom tag settings only for a documented trusted-content boundary.
Keep the safe HTML policy for user-controlled or streamed content.

best_practices: Confirm the repository uses Angular before changing integration code.
Keep HTML sanitization and Mermaid strict mode enabled for untrusted content.
Install optional peers only when the requested feature requires them.
anti_patterns: Do not disable HTML safety for user-controlled Markdown.
Do not apply streaming pacing to already complete history content.
Do not introduce NgModule patterns unless the existing application requires them.

faq.question: Does this skill support standalone Angular components?
faq.answer: Yes. It prefers standalone component imports and signal-friendly examples.

faq.question: When should I add KaTeX styles?
faq.answer: Add KaTeX styles only when the application enables math rendering.

faq.question: How should live chat messages be configured?
faq.answer: Use content binding, smooth streaming, and a final state when the stream completes.

faq.question: How should saved chat history be rendered?
faq.answer: Disable smooth pacing for complete content and use fade if desired.

faq.question: Can I use trusted HTML mode?
faq.answer: Only for a documented, genuinely trusted content surface after security review.

faq.question: Does the skill validate the application?
faq.answer: It recommends the smallest useful Angular development or build command.
